$comment: Golden targets for the VMOS Edge fleet. check-drift.mjs compares every live box against these values. The proxy version is NOT recorded here: it is read from infra/magicbox-proxy/package.json (the code IS the source of truth). Three sources, in this order of authority: the vendor's online reference says what exists; a box's MCP catalogue says what the box believes it serves; only a REST probe on the box says what answers on that CBS line.
captured_from: GET /v1/get_hardware_cfg on box-1..4 over the LAN (LAN-first) and https://help.vmosedge.com (image-release-history, firmware-download, ai-reference-container.txt dated 2026-09-11). Prefer get_hardware_cfg over /v1/systeminfo: it reports `model`, `version` (CBS), `kernel_version`, `device_id` and `hwaddr` on ALL boxes, whereas /v1/systeminfo leaves cbs/kernel blank on the 1.1.4.x CBS line (box-2/3/4).

android_image.$comment: Model-independent — the Android image runs on any host model. `golden` is the last image the vendor published WITHOUT a model restriction (17 July 2026; from 24 July every release is L20-only, then K30-only). It is a CANDIDATE: no device runs it yet, and `upgrade_image` recreates the container, so it is validated on ONE parked device first (Phase 2 canary, separate decision) before it becomes the provisioning default. New devices are created on it so they are born fleet-aligned: pass it to MagicBox-Industrial as --image-repository <golden>. This file is the single source of truth for the value; do not re-hardcode it in the provisioning repo.
android_image.distribution: POST /v1/import_image (multipart upload of the vendor .tar.gz, NDJSON progress) over the LAN — 3.4 GB per box, minutes on the LAN against hours through the tunnel. No export endpoint exists.

vendor_by_model.$comment: The fleet spans TWO hardware families that do NOT share a kernel: box-1..4 are `L1` (Rockchip RK3588S, firmware files named *marsbox*), box-5 is `K1` hardware although its API reports `model = E1.01` (its kernel is 2.0.57_k1, firmware files named *k1*). Keys are the API `model` strings because that is what check-drift matches on. Pushing one family's firmware to the other is how you brick a box: read `model` from /v1/get_hardware_cfg before anything. L1 targets = the LAST versions the vendor published for L1 (every later release is L20/K30-only).

L1.cbs_notes: Fixed cloud devices getting stuck during startup; fixed partial failures of concurrent batch backup restoration; local multimedia upload with gallery broadcast.
L1.cbs_fallback_notes: Embedded in the last L1 firmware image update_2.0.61_marsbox_20260703.img — proven on L1 by the vendor.
L1.kernel_constraint: Vendor release note of 5 June 2026: CBS >= 1.1.6.5 requires kernel >= 2.0.57. box-1 violates it today (CBS 1.1.6.12.1 on kernel 1.0.86_marsbox / Linux 5.10). No kernel-only image exists to go back to 2.0.30: the kernel step is one-way (the only way back is a full firmware flash, which erases data).
L1.full_firmware_latest: update_2.0.61_marsbox_20260703.img (kernel 2.0.61, CBS 1.1.7.2.1) — full flash, ERASES ALL DATA, never used on a populated box

E1.01.hardware: K1 (the API model string is misleading; firmware files are named *k1*)
E1.01.$comment: box-5 is out of scope for the September 2026 session (tunnel down since 21 Sep, absent from the LAN). Baseline = highest version observed on it; the vendor's K1 line went to kernel 2.0.61 / CBS 1.1.7.2.1 (update_2.0.61_k1_20260703.img) — revisit when the box is back.

vendor_upgrade_path.$comment: The vendor layer IS upgradable through the official API — done on box-2/3/4 on 26 September 2026 (~12 min per box, no data touched). Order per box: freeze (maintenance window, 0 containers running, no job or task due), pre-flight (model, our own copy of the running cbs_go), update_kernel (host reboots — 90 s to 3 min; the DHCP lease MAY change: find the box by MAC, never by the old IP), verify kernel_version, update_cbs (cbs_go restarts in ~25 s and leaves cbs_go.backup = the previous binary), verify version + list_names unchanged, two serial boots with boot_ms, /stream-ready, v2 base/version_info, /proxy-test; close the window; record in FLEET-ALIGNMENT.md.
vendor_upgrade_path.cbs: POST /v1/update_cbs (multipart, file named cbs_go_edge_<version>, optional .cbs suffix); rollback = cbs_go.backup next to the binary (and /root/upgrades/cbs/*/cbs_go.pre-upgrade on box-1)
vendor_upgrade_path.kernel: POST /v1/update_kernel (multipart, .img — the host reboots afterwards); NO rollback image for L1 2.0.30
vendor_upgrade_path.safety_net: NONE from the vendor on this firmware: /disk_migration/v1/* answers 404 on both CBS lines (measured 25 Sep 2026). What protects the data is that update_kernel and update_cbs do not touch the NVMe (/container_nswc_lv) nor the overlay upper (/userdata) — measured on three boxes: 57 + 126 + 73 containers intact, our /opt and /etc layer intact.
vendor_upgrade_path.constraint: Match the hardware model. Read `model` from /v1/get_hardware_cfg before pushing anything. One box at a time, canary box-2 first, box-1 only with a written vendor confirmation of the kernel-only path from 1.0.86.

leaves cbs_go.backup = the previous binary next to itself

host_disk.$comment: Disk headroom is a production gate, not a nicety. box-1 reached 98% on /container_nswc_lv in June 2026: guest ext4 writes began failing with EIO (superblock: ext4_check_bdev_write_error, 13 Jun 2026), 44 of its 96 containers took the filesystem error flag, and its job success rate sat at 31% against 70% on a healthy box. Container data.img files are sparse and grow-only — the loop devices are not mounted with discard — so allocation never shrinks on its own. The eMMC root (26 GB) is watched too: box-1 sat at 77% on 25 Sep 2026 from unused images and unrotated logs.
host_disk.reclaim: SSD: offline maintenance pass (e2fsck -fy, purge /tombstones + /anr + /local/tmp/scd.log, mount -o loop,discard, fstrim) — 129 GB recovered on box-1 in August 2026. eMMC: GET /v1/prune_images (unused Android images, 3–6 GB), journald/rsyslog/mihomo bounded by deploy.sh (files/journald.conf.d, files/logrotate.d).

host_hygiene.$comment: What deploy.sh converges on every box and check-drift verifies over SSH. Host OS (Debian 11) is vendor firmware: no apt upgrade, only the logrotate package is installed by us.
host_hygiene.swappiness_note: Android guests run privileged and their init.rc writes /proc/sys/vm/swappiness=100; on kernel 5.10 (box-1) the write reaches the host, on 6.1 it does not (measured 25 Sep 2026). attila-sysctl.timer re-asserts 10 every minute until every host is on 6.1.
host_hygiene.root_password_locked_note: Gated: --lock-root-password installs files/sshd_config.d/60-attila.conf after a key login is verified. The vendor's cbs_debug user keeps its password.

runtime.$comment: Our layer on the host, pinned and shipped by deploy.sh (canary box-2 → 1 → 3 → 4). Checksums verified on 2026-09-25 from nodejs.org SHASUMS256.txt and a downloaded GitHub release asset.

node.note: The nodesource Node 20.20.2 under /usr/bin (EOL 30 April 2026) is left in place and used by nothing once the unit points at /opt/node.

cloudflared.install: dpkg -i, restarted DETACHED (systemd-run --on-active=2s) when the deploy rides the tunnel

reference_capacity.$comment: Fleet policy (2026-07-07): max_concurrent_containers = 10 on every box — the VMOS host ceiling (AGENTS.md). Proven on box-5 at 16 GB RAM; box-2/3/4 have the same 16 GB and box-1 has 32 GB, so 10 is safe fleet-wide. operator_reserve stays 1 (the automator uses max-1). check-drift flags divergence from this value. Measured 9 Sep 2026: the API accepts an 11th run — the ceiling is enforced by our arbiter only.

control_api_minimums.$comment: Floor required by the Android Control API v2 (input/click, accessibility/dump, node find-and-act). Source: help.vmosedge.com/en/sdk/agent-api. The whole fleet already exceeds these. Note that the v2 AGENT version tracks the Android image, not the host CBS: images 20260417 carry agent 1.1.1, images 20260511 and 20260626 carry 1.1.3 (131 vs 137 endpoints, strictly additive).
